public_rationale: He said that in mid-2023 AI could not realistically replace a writer or a writers' room. Sources from the strike period agree. A futurist who advises Hollywood said AI could not effectively cross the picket line on most projects. At most, she thought it could produce a partial draft for humans to finish. A talent lawyer said AI was not an existential threat to writers 'today'. A Fox executive bullish on AI put its ability to do this work years away. No source showed a studio actually replacing writers with AI in this period. Studios' interest in AI shows intent, not ability. On the plain reading, the claim holds.
limitations: The evidence is mostly expert opinion, not a formal capability test.
The sources date from early in the strike (May 2023), not right before the August 3 post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of August 2023, AI cannot realistically replace a writer or a writers' room.

statement.excerpt: AI isn’t currently at a place (nor do I believe it will be for some time) where it could realistically replace a writer or writer’s room

from_speaker: AI isn't currently at a place
where it could realistically replace a writer or writer's room
said about the WGA strike, which he says started with his assumption that Hollywood would cave
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in mid-2023, AI tools such as ChatGPT/GPT-4 could not realistically do the job of a professional Hollywood screenwriter or a writers' room, meaning produce usable scripts without human writers.
Target period: from the start of the WGA strike (May 2023), which he ties to his view, to the post date (2023-08-03). He gives no narrower window, so the whole strike period up to the post counts.
His side remark 'nor do I believe it will be for some time' is a vague forecast with no deadline. It is not scored here.
criteria.support_condition: Credible sources from the period, including industry experts, studio-side figures, or documented production practice, show that AI could not yet realistically replace screenwriters or writers' rooms, and no production is shown to have replaced writers with AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented evidence from the period that a studio or production actually replaced a writer or writers' room with AI-generated scripts for produced work, or credible demonstrations that AI could do this at a professional level.

evidence.explanation: Amy Webb, a futurist who advises Hollywood clients, judged during the strike that AI could not effectively replace striking writers on most projects. At most, she thought it could produce a partial draft that humans would finish. This matches his claim.

evidence.locator: paragraph beginning 'The WGA is the first labor organization'
evidence.explanation: The talent lawyer who warned that some people were trying to get AI to write scripts still said AI was not an existential threat to writers at that time.

evidence.locator: paragraph quoting Fox Entertainment CEO Rob Wade, under 'Not just scripts'
evidence.explanation: Even a studio-side executive bullish on AI put its ability to do writing and other creative work years away. That implies it could not do so in 2023.

evidence.explanation: Context. Writers doubted AI could do their jobs, but AFP reports that studios appeared to believe it could. A belief is not shown capability, so this item does not settle the claim either way.
